source.title: Unveiling Entity-Level Unlearning for Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Analysis
source.authors: Wei-Tao Ma; Xiao-Cheng Feng; Weihong Zhong; Lei Huang; Yang-Fan Ye; Xia-Chong Feng; Bing Qin

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether established unlearning algorithms remove entity-related knowledge, using an entity-level task and evaluation setup rather than the original studies' settings. It does not test recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports entity-target accuracy and model utility after unlearning, which bear on version A. It does not apply fine-tuning as a recovery attack, activation ablation, quantization, or prompting-only attack. Mentioned results from cited work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study runs five unlearning methods (GA, GD, KL, Pref. Opt., NPO-GD) on fictitious TOFU entities in Llama2-7B-Chat and Phi-1.5. It measures target-set multiple-choice accuracy (6 options, chance about 0.17) against model utility. Its central result is that with a realistic, model-constructed forget set, target accuracy stays far above chance, which bears on version A. It also argues that Pref. Opt. induces refusal rather than deletion, because ROUGE collapses while answer likelihood and accuracy stay high; this bears on the 'blocks access' clause of C. It runs no recovery attacks (fine-tuning, quantization, prompting, ablation). It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: current algorithms struggle to erase a whole entity, especially with a constructed forget set; coverage matters; enlarging the set costs utility; fine-tuned entities are more vulnerable than pre-trained ones. Add that the authors argue Pref. Opt. raises refusal likelihood rather than truly forgetting.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates five existing unlearning algorithms in a synthetic entity-level task; it does not implement or test the proposed recovery attacks in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on whether the forget set is the exact target set or a constructed set; increasing forget-set coverage improves forgetting, while increasing its size can reduce model utility. Method and model also affect outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Higher knowledge coverage of the constructed forget set raises forget quality at fixed size. A larger set also raises it but lowers model utility for all methods except Pref. Opt.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Entity-level unlearning effectiveness depends on forget-set knowledge coverage; enlarging the set trades utility for forgetting.

fits_no_version.finding: Knowledge of other fine-tuned entities degrades more during unlearning than pre-trained knowledge does, and fine-tuned entities are more fragile than pre-trained ones (Figure 5, Table 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning results on fine-tuned synthetic entities (e.g. TOFU) may overstate how easily pre-trained knowledge is removed.

record.problems: Experiments use pseudo-entity knowledge injected by fine-tuning, not ordinary pre-training knowledge for the main evaluation; the main results average 20 sampled entities and report no uncertainty estimates. The paper does not measure post-unlearning recovery attacks.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the selected target-accuracy and model-utility results in Tables 1 and 4. Other reported measures (probability, ROUGE, and Forget Quality) are not the target-accuracy or general-ability measures specified by version A.

untested.parts: Whether any recovery attack restores the knowledge; only direct post-unlearning evaluation is done.
All: no relearning or fine-tuning attack.
Activation-direction ablation. Only the refusal-vs-deletion argument for Pref. Opt. is made.
All: no rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context attacks. A fill-in-the-blank retrieval claim is cited from other work only.
All: no new robust method proposed.

missing.what: Pref. Opt. ROUGE vs probability on target set (Llama ROUGE 0.0147 with Prob 0.3486; Phi ROUGE 0.1979 with Prob 0.4323), the core evidence for refusal-not-deletion
Target-set forget quality (KS p-value) per method and forget-set type, e.g. NPO-GD 0.5253 vs 0.0875 on Llama
Pre-trained (celebrity) entity unlearning on Llama2-7B-Base, the only non-synthetic target knowledge in the paper

record.verdict_notes: The accuracy metric is 6-way multiple choice (paraphrase plus 5 perturbations), so chance is about 0.17; 'near chance' was judged against that. Table text extraction scrambles column order. Checks show the 4th numeric column is Forget Q. and the last is Model Utility: the harmonic mean of RS, RAS and WFS reproduces it. The record misread every Phi-1.5 Model Utility row (used WFS) and Llama GA rows R02/R04. All results are means over 20 sampled entities with no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: Whether simple attacks recover knowledge after unlearning; the paper evaluates entity-level unlearning but does not test post-unlearning attacks.
Recovery by fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten examples.
Recovery by activation-direction ablation or evidence that unlearning blocks access rather than deletes knowledge.
Recovery through rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
A newer method's resistance to the specified attacks.

relation.reason: Its own results on five unlearning algorithms bear on versions A and C.

tranche.reason: It reports results and an argument (most methods fail with realistic constructed forget sets; Pref. Opt. raises refusal rather than forgetting) that version A is partial and C holds, in a new entity-level setting. T3 would also be defensible.

source_check.notes: Extracted column order is Prob, ROUGE, Acc, Forget Q., RS, RAS, WFS, Model Utility (MU = harmonic mean of RS/RAS/WFS; Forget Q. confirmed by the text's 0.5253 vs 0.0875). All Phi MU baselines are 0.5414, not 0.5514. Results are means over 20 entities, taken at the step where Forget Quality first peaks. No retrained model's accuracy is reported, so 'near chance' means against uniform 1/6.

statements.correction: Phi-1.5-TOFU, Grad. Ascent, oracle target set: Acc 0.6075 -> 0.2025 (6-way chance ~0.17); Model Utility 0.5414 -> 0.5121; Forget Quality 0.5242. Forget Quality is a KS-test p-value against a reference model not trained on the entity (App. B.4), so the only retrain comparison is distributional. No retrained-model accuracy is reported. On Llama2-7B-Chat, GA/KL reach Acc 0.225/0.2125, but Model Utility falls from 0.6349 to 0.5694/0.5549. With constructed forget sets, Acc stays 0.425-0.60.
statements.problem: The study is cited only through R21 (Phi-1.5, Grad. Ascent, oracle target set) and gives no numbers. R21 is Phi-1.5, not one of the '1-8B Llama models'. Its 6-option accuracy has a chance level (~0.17), against 'measures have no chance level'. 'why' does not list 2406.15796. Most other cells stay well above chance or lose utility, and the authors conclude that methods struggle at entity-level unlearning.
